ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a vertical infinitely long straight wire, with the current direction upward; on the right side of the wire there are two adjacent rectangular coils, the two have the same height, set as h. The left side of rectangle S1 is at a distance a from the wire, and its width is a, so it covers the region where the distance r from the wire is from a to 2a; rectangle S2 is immediately to the right of S1, with width 2a, so it covers the region where r is from 2a to 4a. Reasoning: The magnitude of the magnetic induction intensity of an infinitely long straight wire at a distance r from the wire is B(r)=mu0 I/(2 pi r). The magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane in which the rectangles lie, and on the same side the direction is consistent, therefore the magnetic flux can be integrated according to the horizontal distance. Φ1 = h ∫_a^(2a) mu0 I/(2 pi r) dr = h mu0 I/(2 pi) ln 2. Φ2 = h ∫_(2a)^(4a) mu0 I/(2 pi r) dr = h mu0 I/(2 pi) ln 2. Therefore Φ1/Φ2 = 1.
